question: Select the right bank tributary of the Indus River system.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Kabul River**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Kabul River** is a right-bank tributary of the Indus River, originating in the Hindu Kush Mountains near Maidan Wardak Province in Afghanistan.
 
• It flows through eastern Afghanistan and northern Pakistan before joining the Indus River near the city of Attock in Pakistan.
 
• The river has several tributaries, including the Kunar River, which contributes significantly to its flow.
 
• The Kabul River is an important water source for irrigation and hydroelectric power generation in the region.
 
• It plays a significant role in the socio-economic development of the areas it traverses, especially in Afghanistan and Pakistan.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jhelum River:**

 
 
• The Jhelum River is a left-bank tributary of the Indus River and originates from Verinag Spring in Jammu & Kashmir, India.
 
• It flows through the Kashmir Valley and is an important source of water for agriculture and hydropower in the region.
 
• Major dams on the Jhelum include the Mangla Dam in Pakistan.
 
 
 
• **Ravi River:**
 
 
• The Ravi River is another left-bank tributary of the Indus and originates in Himachal Pradesh, India.
 
• It flows through Punjab (India) and Punjab (Pakistan) before merging with the Chenab River.
 
• The Ravi is one of the five rivers of the Punjab region and is significant for irrigation in both India and Pakistan.
 
 
 
• **Chenab River:**
 
 
• The Chenab River is a left-bank tributary of the Indus River, formed by the confluence of the Chandra and Bhaga rivers in Himachal Pradesh, India.
 
• It flows through Jammu & Kashmir and Punjab (Pakistan) before joining the Indus River.
 
• The river is crucial for agriculture and hydropower in the region, with several dams and barrages constructed on it.
